question: To signal a right turn by hand, you extend your right arm:
options: Horizontally, outside and to the right of the vehicle
explanation: Hand signals are for when no indicator is fitted or working. To turn right, extend the right arm horizontally outside and to the right of the vehicle (Reg. 11(2)(ii)).

hi.question: हाथ से दाएँ मुड़ने का संकेत देने के लिए आप दायाँ हाथ कैसे फैलाते हैं?
options: वाहन के बाहर दाईं ओर क्षैतिज (सीधा)
hi.explanation: जब इंडिकेटर न हो या काम न करे, दाएँ मुड़ने के लिए दायाँ हाथ वाहन के बाहर दाईं ओर क्षैतिज फैलाएँ।

question: Raising your right forearm vertically outside the vehicle, palm to the right, signals that you intend to:
explanation: To signal a stop by hand, raise the right forearm vertically outside and to the right of the vehicle (Reg. 11(2)(i)). The regulation has no separate hand signal for slowing down.

question: You should signal your intention in good time before turning or changing lanes.
explanation: Signal clearly and in good time before changing course or turning (Reg. 11(1), Reg. 8).

en.question: You should signal your intention in good time before turning or changing lanes.

question: Once you have turned, you can leave your indicator on for the rest of the journey.
explanation: Cancel the indicator after the manoeuvre so you do not mislead other road users.

question: An anticlockwise circular motion of the right arm signals that you intend to:
explanation: To signal a left turn by hand, extend the right arm and rotate it anti-clockwise (Reg. 11(2)(iii)).

question: Hazard (four-way) lamps should be used:
options: When your vehicle is a temporary hazard, e.g. breakdown
explanation: When a vehicle breaks down, switch on the hazard warning lights immediately (Reg. 28); hazard lights are also used after a minor accident and when towing (Reg. 29, 30).

question: A solid white line along the centre of the road means:
explanation: Do not drive on or over a single or double solid longitudinal line, except when there is an obstruction (Reg. 6(6)).

question: A broken (dashed) white centre line means:
options: You may cross it when safe
explanation: A broken line may be crossed to overtake when it is safe.

question: Where should you stop at a signal or stop sign with a stop line marked?
explanation: Stop before the stop line at a red signal (Reg. 12(1)(a)) and before the STOP line at a STOP sign (Reg. 7(1)(a)).

question: Wide white stripes across the road parallel to traffic mark a:
explanation: This is a zebra crossing; pedestrians have priority.

question: You may stop on a zebra crossing if the signal ahead is red and the queue is long.
explanation: Do not block a pedestrian crossing even when traffic is stopped (Reg. 39); stop before the stop line (Reg. 12(1)(a)).

explanation: At red, stop before the stop line preceding the pedestrian crossing (Reg. 12(1)(a)).

question: A steady amber (yellow) light means:
options: Stop before the stop line, unless you are too close to stop safely
explanation: At amber, stop before the stop line or crossing, unless you have already crossed it or are too close to stop safely (Reg. 12).

question: A flashing amber light means:
explanation: At flashing amber, slow down and proceed with caution, giving way to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection (Reg. 12(3)(c)).

question: You should dip your headlights when meeting oncoming traffic at night.
explanation: The high beam must be dipped in good time when an oncoming vehicle approaches (Reg. 31(4)).

question: Using the horn is permitted in silence zones near hospitals.
explanation: Unnecessary use of the horn is prohibited (Reg. 23(1)); a silence zone is an area where sound signals are prohibited (Reg. 2(1)(p)).

options: No lamps if road is lit
explanation: Use the required lights at nightfall, at night, at dawn and in poor visibility (Reg. 31).
